text:
[title] Why serving is hard
[body] Every request grows a KV-cache as it generates tokens
[body] Fragmented memory wastes GPU capacity
[body] Tail latency (p99) is what users feel

novice.takeaway: The slide lists three technical reasons why serving large language models efficiently is difficult, related to memory use and response speed.
questions: Why does fragmented memory waste GPU capacity?
What does p99 latency specifically measure?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to understand the core technical challenges their system aims to solve.

peer.takeaway: Serving large language models is difficult because growing memory demands, inefficient memory usage, and tail latency together create performance bottlenecks.
questions: What exactly is a KV-cache in this context?
How does memory fragmentation specifically waste GPU capacity?
How do these three challenges relate to the 2.4x improvement?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to understand these three core challenges motivate their proposed serving improvements.

expert.takeaway: The slide outlines three core challenges in LLM serving—growing KV-cache, memory fragmentation, and tail latency—that motivate the improvement claimed on slide 1.
questions: What technique addresses fragmentation, e.g. PagedAttention-like scheme?
How does the fix target p99 specifically?
expert.inferred_claim: These three problems are the key bottlenecks the presenter's system solves to boost p99 goodput.

metrics.intent: Our serving system delivers 2.4x higher goodput at p99 latency by pairing PagedAttention-style KV-cache management with speculative decoding.
